title: CORS null origin accepted with credentials
desc: API reflected null in Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials:true. Sandboxed iframes send null origin.
steps:
1. Send request with Origin: null
2. Check response: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null + Allow-Credentials: true
3. Host exploit in sandboxed iframe

title: CORS wildcard subdomain trust — subdomain takeover chain
desc: API trusted *.shopify.com. Attacker took over abandoned subdomain and used it to make credentialed cross-origin requests.
steps:
1. Find abandoned subdomain: old.shopify.com
2. Take over subdomain via DNS
3. Host exploit page on subdomain
4. Make credentialed requests to API — CORS allows it

title: CORS origin reflection — any origin trusted
desc: API reflected the Origin header back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials:true. Any origin could make authenticated requests.
steps:
1. Send request with Origin: https://attacker.com
2. Response: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://attacker.com + Allow-Credentials: true
3. Host exploit on attacker.com — steal user data

title: CORS misconfiguration on internal API endpoint
desc: Internal API endpoint had CORS misconfiguration allowing any origin. Exposed internal user data to cross-origin requests.
steps:
1. Find internal API endpoint
2. Send with Origin: https://attacker.com
3. Response allows cross-origin read
4. Steal internal data

title: CORS bypass via pre-domain match
desc: CORS check used startsWith('https://target.com'). Attacker registered target.com.evil.com to bypass the check.
steps:
1. Register domain: target.com.evil.com
2. Send request with Origin: https://target.com.evil.com
3. startsWith check passes — CORS allowed

title: CORS misconfiguration leaks OAuth tokens
desc: OAuth callback endpoint had CORS misconfiguration. Cross-origin request could read the OAuth token from the response.
steps:
1. Identify OAuth callback endpoint
2. Send cross-origin request with credentials
3. Read OAuth token from response
